title: Warning, runtime/fatal errors and stalled operations
prerequisites: Global asynchronous error listeners are active from initialization onward.
sequence: Capture event class, original errorType, errorDescription and unsigned errorCode for Warning, RuntimeError and FatalError.
Record timestamp, current SDK state, pending operation and last relevant event with sensitive fields removed.
Keep the original SDK error separate from an app-created timeout or invalid-state message.
Stop blind retries after a fatal or uncertain state; use the documented recovery/start/restart transition.
If progress stops, present the captured evidence and ask for missing deployment/SDK information.
expected_result: All three error categories are handled.
checklist: All three error categories are handled.
Numeric code and full description survive formatting.
Fatal events are observable even before activation UI appears.
No password, activation code, token or configuration JWT is in the diagnostic log.
failure_handling: Do not guess an error meaning from a numeric code; use version-matched evidence.
GettingStarted sample handlers are not uniformly complete: improve them rather than copying their omissions.

platform_notes.android: The inspected ErrorHandlingModel logs generic runtime/warning messages and lacks a fatal branch in that class; do not copy it as complete diagnostic coverage. The 15.16 events inherit AbstractErrorEvent getters. Java int is signed: use errorCode.toLong() and 0xffffffffL to preserve its unsigned value.
platform_notes.ios: ErrorModel receives KSMWarningEvent, KSMErrorRuntimeEvent and KSMErrorFatalEvent and extracts descriptions/codes. Preserve the original SDK error type too. In the 15.16 delivery, Warning uses errorStatus; RuntimeError/FatalError use errorType. The Objective-C signed int errorCode needs UInt32(bitPattern:) to retain the unsigned 32-bit code.

qualification.note: Source review only for the complete recipe. Example validation is recorded separately and does not qualify live SDK initialization, event delivery or backend flows.

validation.scope: Synthetic Warning/RuntimeError/FatalError instances and unsigned code mapping only; not live SDK initialization or backend flows.
